text: Then, this very morning, Mister Wilson went to work as usual and found the office door shut and locked. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of the door was a small card that said, The Red Headed League is dissolved, October 9, 1890. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes and I looked at the card and at the sad face behind it, and we both burst out laughing. <break time="0.8s" /> Wilson asked the landlord, who said that he had never heard of the League or of anyone called Duncan Ross. <break time="0.8s" /> The red headed man in that office, he said, was a lawyer named William Morris who had moved out the day before. <break time="0.8s" /> Wilson went to the new address, but he found that it was a factory that made artificial kneecaps. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes then asked whether the assistant was a small, quick man with no hair on his face and a white splash of acid on his forehead. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, sir, cried Wilson in surprise, and Holmes sat up in his chair with great excitement. <break time="0.8s" /> After Wilson left, Holmes said that it was quite a three pipe problem and asked me not to speak to him for fifty minutes. <break time="0.8s" /> He curled up in his chair with his knees drawn up to his nose, and he sat smoking in silence like a strange bird.
